clue.text: Where cargo goes bottoms up

definitions.meaning: cargo is lowered through the opening in a ship's deck into the hold
a drinking toast urging everyone to drain the glass

explanation.surface: A tipsy shipping joke: freight being loaded while the crew raise a toast.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works literally (into a ship's hold) and as the cheery toast said before downing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the route freight takes below deck and a toast before swallowing a drink in one go.

clue.text: Porter, we hear, finally caught sleeping

indicators.note: says the porter word aloud and spells it by its sound

parts.note: a doorman is a hotel porter

indicators.note: takes the last letter of caught

explanation.surface: A hotel porter is reportedly caught dozing on duty at last.
explanation.walkthrough: DOORMAN said aloud gives DORMAN; 'finally' adds the T at the end of 'caught'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dormant is inactive or resting, as in a hibernating animal or a volcano asleep.

clue.text: He can drive and lay about bowling

indicators.note: the bet word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to lay is to bet, a wager
a cricket bowler who is bowling is said to be on

explanation.surface: Someone who can both drive and spread a bet around on the bowling green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal. In cricket a bowler currently bowling is said to be on; 'drive' means driving a horse-drawn cart, not a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagoner is the driver of a horse-drawn goods cart.

clue.text: Conspicuous, being three foot high

indicators.note: high in the sense of drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Something very noticeable because it stands three feet tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' looks like a measurement but means intoxicated, signalling a rearrangement of THREE FOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prominent and in plain view means being at the front of things.

clue.text: "Forty." said the Romans. ", are outstandingly good"

indicators.note: the Roman numeral for the number is spoken aloud letter by letter, ex and el

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Romans declaring that people aged forty are excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Romans wrote forty as XL; read out as letters, ex-el, it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To be superior and stand out in quality is to surpass others.

clue.text: Extent of the land engineers covered with a prison

indicators.note: the engineers are enclosed by the jail letters

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Army engineers covering a piece of ground with a prison building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered with' is the container signal; the Royal Engineers are a British Army corps, a crossword favourite for the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is land area measured in acres.

clue.text: Where beacon burnt — a hilltop round the Kent area

indicators.note: the hilltop word goes around the area letters

parts.note: the crest is the top of a hill
Kent is a county in south-east England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A signal fire on a summit in the Kent countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is the container signal. Kent is the English county in the south-east corner, hence the compass abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cresset is an iron basket or cup holding burning fuel, used as a torch or signal fire.

clue.text: Throw doubt upon evangelist?

parts.note: to question something is to doubt it
Mark is one of the four gospel writers

explanation.surface: Casting doubt on a gospel writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue ends with the very symbol it describes; the whole clue is both wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation symbol placed after a query, which ends this very clue.

clue.text: Just a piano

definitions.meaning: just in the sense of honest and fair
a type of piano with vertical strings, as opposed to a grand

explanation.definitionFit: A just person is honourable and principled; an instrument with its frame standing vertically is one kind of piano.

clue.text: One can hardly be seen in pink eye-piece

indicators.note: the remaining letters go inside the shade word

parts.note: coral is a pinkish-red shade

indicators.note: the round O of the word one, a nought next to nothing, drops out of sight here

parts.note: the word one, spelt out

explanation.surface: Someone almost invisible in a pink eyeglass, or a remark about a barely visible lens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can hardly be seen' makes the nought-like O vanish from 'One', and 'in' is the container signal. The cornea is the clear, nearly invisible front piece of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Corneal relates to the cornea, the transparent covering at the front of the eye, so a part of the eye.

clue.text: Potted ten reds in all — get the picture?

indicators.note: in snooker, potting balls sends them scattering, and here the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A snooker player potting all ten red balls, then asked if you follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potted' rearranges TEN REDS IN ALL. The definition is a pun: an old glass plate projected as a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass transparency projected onto a screen by a magic lantern produced an image to view.

clue.text: In Scotland, lac entails a change

indicators.note: a change of order rearranges the letters of the word before it

parts.note: the word entails, taken letter for letter as the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A remark that a Scottish custom involves some alteration.
explanation.walkthrough: The held clue misreads '1ac' (1 across, the toast DOWN THE HATCH) as 'lac'. 'a change' rearranges ENTAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gaelic word for good health is the drinking toast raised in Scotland, the local equivalent of a cheers before a dram.

clue.text: It thickens soup a bit on the side

definitions.meaning: in cookery, a mixture of egg yolk and cream used to bind and thicken sauces and soups

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a culinary term for an egg-and-cream binding agent and also an extramarital affair.

clue.text: In theory, no others are put underground

indicators.note: keep one letter and lose the next, so every other letter of theory is struck out

explanation.surface: A claim that, in principle, nobody else gets buried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no others' takes alternate letters of THEORY (T, E, R), after IN given as it is. 'In theory' looks like a phrase meaning hypothetically.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury a body is to place it in a grave below the earth.

clue.text: Eccentric, bizarre offer involving very little money

indicators.note: the jumbled letters wrap around the money word
something bizarre is strange and twisted, so the letters of offer are jumbled

parts.note: a cent is a coin of tiny value

explanation.surface: An odd, outlandish proposal for a trivial sum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bizarre' scrambles 'offer' (to OFFRE) and 'involving' wraps it around the coin word. 'Eccentric' is literally off the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not placed at the middle is literally eccentric, away from the centre point.

clue.text: Whence, proverbially, one may go from bad to worse on the range

definitions.text: Whence, proverbially, one may go from bad to worse on the range

parts.words: Whence, proverbially, one may go from bad to worse on the range
parts.note: the saying about leaving a bad spot only to land in the fire, with a cooking range as the stove

explanation.surface: A proverb about trouble getting worse, set on a kitchen stove.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb runs 'out of the ... into the fire'; 'range' is a kitchen stove, not a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallow pan for cooking food in hot fat on a stove, the starting point in the proverb.

clue.text: No fear of skirt being worn back to front, see

annotationWithheld.why: No fear of skirt being worn back to front, see (3,6): the only parse is NO + KILT reversed + ELY, so 'No' is both the start of the definition 'No fear' and the letters NO, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: No fear of skirt being worn back to front, see

clue.text: He prepares a horse shoe

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a coach of racehorses and a training shoe such as a sneaker.

clue.text: One can have incorporated German figures of speech

parts.note: I is one as a Roman numeral

indicators.note: the permission word takes the language abbreviation into its body

parts.note: may expresses permission, like can

explanation.surface: Someone allowed to work German words into their rhetoric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have incorporated' is the container signal; 'One' giving I and 'can' giving the permission word are both easy to read past.
explanation.definitionFit: Imagery is figurative language, metaphors and similes collectively.

clue.text: Shelter around container

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means around or about
a bin is a receptacle

explanation.surface: A hut set up near a storage tub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal but gives CA (circa).
explanation.definitionFit: A small hut or hut-like room gives refuge, a simple form of shelter.

clue.text: Murderer captured — likely to be this officer

indicators.note: the murderer's name holds the other piece inside it

parts.note: Cain, in Genesis, killed his brother Abel
apt means likely or inclined

explanation.surface: A killer has been arrested, probably by a senior officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captured' is the container signal; Cain, who killed Abel in Genesis, is the Bible's first murderer.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is a rank of commissioned officer in the army or navy.

clue.text: Firemen give ship assistance, we hear

indicators.note: the two words spoken together give the sound of the answer

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted ship and aid is assistance

explanation.surface: Firefighters helping a boat in trouble, so the story goes.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIG plus AID, spoken aloud, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire brigade is the organised body of firefighters in a district.

clue.text: Firm had a man they kept under cover

indicators.note: the letters are concealed inside the words had a man they

explanation.surface: A company sheltered a man, perhaps a fugitive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' reads as a noun (a business) but is the adjective meaning resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unyielding and resolute in an opinion means standing firm.

clue.text: Animal revered by family, a cat without 40 per cent of teeth

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the cat goes round

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: two letters out of five, the first two of teeth

explanation.surface: A sacred clan creature, a cat that has lost much of its bite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the cat goes round the letters; teeth has five letters, so 40 per cent is the first two.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a natural object or creature adopted as an emblem by a clan and held in reverence.

clue.text: Back most of non-clerics to make a joke of marriage

indicators.note: back here turns the whole joined string round so it reads from right to left
the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the laity are people who are not clergy
a pun is a joke on words

explanation.surface: Advice to turn your back on lay people and mock the wedded state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims the final letter of the lay-people word, and 'Back' turns the whole joined string round.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to weddings or wedlock.

clue.text: Most affectionate family that's short of a leader

parts.note: kin are relatives

indicators.note: a word short of its leader is missing the letter at its head, so the expansion of that's loses its opening letter

parts.note: i.e., Latin id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Praise for a loving family who happen to lack a head of the household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' expands to ID EST (the Latin behind i.e.), and 'short of a leader' removes its I, leaving DEST.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of kind, meaning gentle and warm-hearted to the greatest degree.

clue.text: Bill's American partner left Bill imprisoned

definitions.note: Bill is: the 's stands for is, linking definition and wordplay

indicators.note: the left-and-bill letters are locked up inside the partner word

parts.note: pard is American slang for a partner, from pardner
AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Bill's Yankee sidekick has abandoned him in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The two Bills look like a man's name: one is a poster, the other an account. 'imprisoned' locks the left and account letters inside the partner slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill is a printed notice posted up in public, the same as a poster.

clue.text: Broadcast in emergency by English power behind the throne

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A message aired during a national crisis by some English official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' rearranges IN EMERGENCY to make GREYEMINENC, and E for English completes it. The phrase comes from Père Joseph, Cardinal Richelieu's grey-robed adviser.
explanation.definitionFit: An adviser who wields real influence unseen, while someone else holds the official title.
